blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal. The reports count condos and townhomes together in one line, so this table cannot separate the two. Shares are this community’s count divided by the Maple Ridge total for condos and townhomes that month.

blocks.text: Condo buildings in East Central
Rosewood Court — 22611 116 Avenue

Built 1991, 81 units (building directory, secondary source). The directory records restrictions as: age restrictions, pets allowed with restrictions, rentals not allowed — the rental line is void since November 24, 2022. Directory amenities: club house, exercise centre, in-suite laundry, indoor pool, recreation centre, workshop. Listings describe a 55+ retirement community in Fraserview Village, strata fees covering hot water and gas, and underground parking.
Emerald Manor — 11609 227 Street

Built 1997 per current listings, which describe an accessible 55+ retirement community in Fraserview Village; one listing records construction as "Concrete, Frame Wood, Mixed (Exterior), Stucco" and another describes concrete and metal frame construction. Gas and hot water are included in the strata fee per listings; a guest suite and possible RV parking are also described. Unit count: Not confirmed (no directory page found). Restrictions beyond the published 55+ positioning: Not confirmed.
The Willows — 11578 225 Street

Built 1987 per current listings, marketed "for those 55 and better" in Fraserview Village. Listings describe it as pet friendly — two cats or two dogs (or one of each) — with the strata fee covering use of the Fraserview Village amenity building plus gas, secure underground parking, across from Brickwood Park. Unit count: Not confirmed.
Castlemount — 11601 227 Street

Listings name it "Castlemount at Fraserview Village," a 55+ community with access to the village clubhouse, exercise facilities, indoor pool and workshop, and Fraser River views from some units. Year built and unit count: Not confirmed from the sources checked.
Riverside — 11510 225 Street
Built 1988 and described as a 55+ community in a current listing. Unit count, construction and restrictions: Not confirmed.
Podium — 11655 Fraser Street

Built 2024, 125 units (building directory, secondary source). The presale record describes a 6-storey wood-frame project by Whitetail Homes at 116 Avenue made up of 120 condos plus 5 townhomes — so the directory's 125-unit figure appears to count both forms; the townhomes are part of the same project and are not separate apartment condos. Restrictions: Not confirmed.
Brickwater Village (Brickwater at The Village) — 227 Street / Selkirk Avenue area, by Falcon Homes

A mixed-use project of four buildings with four storeys of homes over ground-floor commercial and "200+ condominiums" project-wide (presale source, secondary); Phase 3 alone was marketed at 44 condos. Individual building addresses and years from current listings: 22633 Selkirk Avenue (built 2024, marketed as "Brickwater 4"), 11865 227 Street (built 2022), 11893 227 Street (built 2019), 22638 119 Avenue (built 2020). Restrictions: Not confirmed generally; one listing aggregator records cats OK at 11893 227 Street — that is listing-level data, not a verified building bylaw summary.
Highpointe (also spelled "Highpoint" in some listings) — 11641 227 Street

Built 2024. A building-directory listing page records the complex name as Highpointe, strata plan EPS9270, and the unit as one of 35 units at the address (building directory, secondary source). Listings describe a Concordia Homes building of concrete and steel construction with a guest suite, bike storage and a car/dog wash. Restrictions: Not confirmed.
Station One — 12070 227 Street
Named in current East Central apartment listings. Year built, unit count and restrictions: Not confirmed.
Sierra Ridge — 11703 Fraser Street
Unit count, construction and restrictions: Not confirmed.

items.t: The downtown part of the sub-area is covered by the City's Town Centre Area Plan.

Where the condo stock concentrates, in two clusters: (1) the Fraserview Village 55+ cluster on and around 116 Avenue and 225–227 Streets (Rosewood Court, Emerald Manor, The Willows, Castlemount, Riverside); (2) the downtown/Haney stock along Fraser Street and 227 Street, including the Brickwater buildings and the new Podium and Highpointe buildings.
Transit anchors: Haney Place Exchange with the R3 RapidBus, and Port Haney Station at 22300 River Road on the West Coast Express.

The City's own name for the Brickwater development location is "Brickwater" (a sample address in City material is 11897 227 Street); City pages do not state the building type, which comes from developer and listing sources.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in East Central

items.t: Transit-Oriented Areas: Maple Ridge's TOA Bylaw No. 8001-2024 designates the Haney Place Exchange and Port Haney Station areas — the policy frame behind the new downtown density at Podium, Brickwater and Highpointe.

Flood and escarpment rules on the south edge: along the River Road/Port Haney edge the flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic and Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibits secondary suites on floodplain properties; the escarpment policy area's east boundary is 224 Street, and a geotechnical report is required within 300 m of the escarpment crest.

blocks.text: Good to know about East Central

items.t: Four separate strata corporations share one amenity building. Rosewood Court, Emerald Manor, The Willows and Castlemount are distinct buildings/stratas marketed together as Fraserview Village, and the amenity building (indoor pool, hot tub, clubhouse, guest suite) is a village facility — a unit's fee and voting rights sit with its own strata, not the village.

The village's published data is uneven. Rosewood Court is the only Fraserview building with a full directory record (1991, 81 units). Emerald Manor's build year (1997) and The Willows' (1987) come from listings, and no public source checked publishes unit counts for Emerald Manor, The Willows or Castlemount — budget for a Form B and strata-documents order to get the real numbers.

Two of the "condo" counts downtown blend forms. Podium's 125 directory units include 5 townhomes, and Brickwater's "200+ condominiums" is a four-building project total, not a single building — compare per-building counts only from strata plans.

The escarpment rules reach into East Central. The escarpment policy area's east boundary is 224 Street and a geotechnical report is required within 300 m of the crest — relevant to any future redevelopment or addition on the slope-side streets above the river, even though the existing condo buildings predate the policy.

A second rapid link is planned, not built. TransLink's Langley–Haney Place BRT is in detailed planning (22 km, 10-minute peak headways) with timelines not determined — price downtown units on today's R3 and West Coast Express service, not the BRT.

Maple Ridge's OCP citation is unsettled in current sources (Bylaw 7060-2014 vs 7998-2024, update adopted November 25, 2025) — quote planning policy for a specific building from a current City document, not from memory.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in East Central
The Fraserview Village buildings a buyer will assume are townhouses are apartment-form strata; they are carried below in their true form and are NOT counted.
Streets, schools and getting around East Central

items.t: The City publishes no boundary for the MLS sub-area; the wider sub-area takes in the residential streets east and north of downtown toward 232 Street and 124 Avenue.

Where the townhouse stock actually sits: along the 116 Avenue corridor south of downtown — Fraser Glen (22740), Dogwood Lane (22555) and Duet (22977) — plus Gold Creek Estates on 228 Street and Alouette Estates at the east edge on 232 Street. The apartment stock concentrates in the Town Centre along 224, 226 and 227 Streets and 121 Avenue.

Transit: Haney Place Exchange is in this sub-area (routes include the R3, 701, 733, 741, 743, 744, 745, 746, 748, 749 and 791); the R3 Lougheed Hwy RapidBus runs from Coquitlam Central Station to Haney Place; Port Haney Station, 22300 River Road, runs weekday West Coast Express trains between Waterfront and Mission City.

That figure COMBINES condos and townhomes; SnapStats publishes no townhome-only figure. Maple Ridge community-level Condos & Townhomes median was $525,000 in September 2026; no sub-area median is published.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in East Central

items.t: OCP citation — CONTESTED, flagged, never resolved: The Town Centre Area Plan (OCP s. 10.4) covers the west end; its update expanded boundaries to incorporate River Bend, consolidated designations and added a Town Centre Core designation supporting higher densities around the Haney Transit Exchange and Port Haney Station; Transit-Oriented Area Designation Bylaw No. 8001-2024 covers those two TOAs.

Flood and escarpment: along River Road / Port Haney the flood construction level is 6.7 m geodetic (including freeboard), no habitable floor space may sit below it on affected lots, a covenant on title identifies floodplain construction, and Zoning Bylaw s. 402.8(h) prohibits rental accommodation (suites) on floodplain properties; the Fraser River Escarpment policy area's east boundary is 224 Street, and lots within 300 m of the crest require a geotechnical report on a Section 219 covenant before a building permit. The 116 Avenue townhouse corridor sits north of the river flats, but status is per-lot.

blocks.text: Good to know about East Central

items.t: That is why tenures and unit counts here carry not confirmed labels other sub-areas do not need.
Any page or note still calling it proposed is stale.

Four separate strata corporations share one amenity building at Fraserview Village — indoor pool, hot tub, clubhouse, guest suite — so two units a block apart can carry different pet bylaws and different CRF positions while sharing the same pool. Compare building by building, never by the village name.

The newest seniors stock downtown is not for sale, and the 55+ strata supply is 1990s stock: the Town Centre's recent growth (Podium, Brickwater, Highpointe, the TOA framework under Bylaw No. 8001-2024) is general-market product.

The escarpment rules reach into East Central: the policy area's east boundary is 224 Street and a geotechnical report on a Section 219 covenant is required within 300 m of the crest — relevant to additions and rebuilds on the slope-side streets, even though the existing complexes predate the policy.

blocks.text: East Central home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

114 condos sold in East Central with a median price of $482,500 (the middle half sold between $400,000 and $557,500), taking a median of 28 days to sell at 97.3% of the last list price; 3% sold above list. They had a median $540 per square foot, a median year built of 2008 and a median strata fee of $380 a month. 71 townhomes sold in East Central with a median price of $700,000 (the middle half sold between $625,000 and $762,500), taking a median of 24 days to sell at 98.0% of the last list price; 7% sold above list. They had a median $479 per square foot, a median year built of 1997 and a median strata fee of $393 a month.
